text: The current category system that is doing letter based categories. that shit sucks. it is a bad habit carried on from a demo that lived outside of the internal editor. you should change it so that its not so silly
resolution: Killed the letter-based category system in the internal editor's texture catalog. The rail was grouping materials by the effect_fills demo's authoring batches — 'A · Environment', 'B · Condemned', … 'J · Wall Props' — letter-prefixed boards that were a habit carried in from that standalone eval cart; the batch letter tells a world-builder nothing about where a material belongs. Replaced it in cart/hmsc-int/game/textures/shaders.ts with a purpose-based taxonomy keyed by material slug (TEXTURE_CATEGORIES + CATEGORY_BY_SLUG): Ground & Roads, Walls & Masonry, Building Facades, Wall Props, Floors & Interiors, Surfaces & Glass, Cloth & Materials, Objects & Clutter, Stencils. fillSpec now sets group = textureCategory(slug); the ROAD and Cutout Stencil one-offs moved to Ground & Roads / Stencils; shaderGroups() sorts the rail by the declared category order. Crucially the material IDs are untouched (a-brick, i-brick-apartment, …) — letter/board still drive the stable id and the demo swatch layout, so stored materials and references keep resolving; only the visible grouping changed. effect_fills (the demo, which lives outside the editor) keeps its A–J letter boards since that cart IS a board-layout evaluator. Verified: shaders.ts transpiles; the workbench materials (6/6), buildings (22/22), and cutout (10/10) P4 suites all pass against the new catalog. Did not touch catalog.ts/chooser.ts (another session's in-flight untracked files).
